BUCKET (added 2026-09-23 by the product owner): percentages beside the ANALYZE level counts. Agreed design after measurement, not the raw version: whole numbers (one reading is 0.7% of the sample, so a decimal implies resolution the data lacks); the distinct-day count printed beside the reading count (145 readings spanned only 25 local days, so the standard error on the 47% share is 10.0 pp by days against 4.3 pp by readings); and a 'close to even' line when the increased/decreased gap is under about two standard errors on the day count. At 3.13% the split was 47/43 -- 0.4 SE, a coin flip that a bare percentage would make look like a lean. At 2.29% it was 70/25 on 20 days, 4.5 SE, and that call came true at +1.68 pp. The later half of the idea -- how often the section was right, conditioned on the news at the time -- is calibration (z = +2.23 day level, needs about 171 independent days, we have 42) and news conditioning is two gates beyond that. SP_C_HANDOFF.md section 31. SP-C.15 (2026-09-21): replaced the decision engine's valuation leg. valuation_state had been CHEAP on 364/364 rows because its fixed -1.5 threshold sat 0.02 pp outside the observed range of 438 readings, so the first input to the conflict matrix carried no information. It is now a rank over the settled non-user window, with a direction gate: CHEAP also requires the reading to be below fair value and EXPENSIVE requires it above, because a percentile-EXPENSIVE reading means 'less discounted than usual' and the matrix turns EXPENSIVE + WEAKENING into SELL -- on rank alone the engine would have sold a market trading 1.6% below fair value. Below MIN_OBSERVATIONS the answer is UNKNOWN and the matrix abstains; there is deliberately no fixed-threshold fallback. Replayed over 366 decisions: CHEAP 366 -> CHEAP 111/FAIR 222/UNKNOWN 33, BUY 131 -> 63. Also fixed the config keys valuation.py had been reading that do not exist (the configured sell threshold of 3.0 had never been in effect) and ANALYZE's projected clean-from date, which was a day early. Recorded in SP_C_HANDOFF.md section 26.
